title: Kilo Code Pricing 2026: Plans and Token Costs
summary: Kilo code pricing varies by plan and model. This comparison shows the cost of each option to help you decide which works for your budget.
body_markdown:
## Kilo Code Model List With Per-Token Costs


$0.10 to $2 per million tokens is the range of input prices across the models Kilo routes to, according to[Sovyron's Kilo listing](https://sovyron.com/providers/kilo/) ., so your model choice moves the bill more than any line Kilo itself adds.

### Gateway credits versus your own API keys


With gateway credits, you prepay Kilo and each request draws down the balance at the listed per-token rate.


With your own API keys, the model provider invoices you directly and Kilo's list is only a guide to what you'll owe them. Either way, the arithmetic's the same: tokens times rate.


Take one run that sends 200,000 input tokens:


- On Claude Haiku 5.5 at[Narev](https://www.narev.ai/docs/hub/providers/kilo) 's $0.10 per million, that's $0.02
- On GPT Latest at $2 per million, it's $0.40
- Run it 100 times a day and the gap's $2 versus $40 in input cost alone, before any output tokens
- The cheaper option deserves serious consideration


### Model table with input and output rates


Before you set a default model and forget it, see where it sits: six models have confirmed input prices, and the table orders them cheapest first.

At $0.10 in and $0.50 out per million, **Haiku 5.5 is the floor** , which makes it the sensible choice for classification, extraction and routing.[Sovyron](https://sovyron.com/providers/kilo/) calculates that GLM 5.3 FlashX at $0.37 costs 3.7 times as much as Haiku for the same input.


According to Sovyron, GPT-6.1 Terra at $1 is ten times Haiku's rate, so reserve it for work that needs its visual reasoning or computer use.


Sovyron observes that GLM-5.2 at $1.40 and Gemini Omni Flash at $1.50 sit close together, so a switch between them barely changes your bill.


At $2, GPT Latest is the most expensive on this list, so a long-context agent loop on it adds up fastest.


I have no confirmed context windows or Kilo markup figures for these rows.


Check each on the provider's page before you budget on them, because output tokens usually cost more than input and an agent that writes a lot of code leans on them.


### Free and promotional models: what to rely on


Budget every one of the six models above at its listed rate, because none is flagged free in the source. If Kilo's picker shows a free or promotional model, treat it as a trial, not a plan.


When a promotion ends, a workflow built on a zero price turns into a line item that same day.


Test the free model if you like, but price the same job on Haiku 5.5 first, so you know what the bill becomes when the promotion stops.
